methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates multiple lines of evidence (TCGA screening, validation in clinical specimens, in vitro assays, and xenograft models) and includes mechanistic rescue experiments linking the CAV2 phenotype to the PACT-PKR axis (Methods 2.1–2.2; Results 3.4–3.7). Animal work describes randomization for treatment assignment and specifies dosing schedules for Cetuximab in an orthotopic model (2.2). However, some cohort descriptions appear internally inconsistent in the narrative (e.g., statements about numbers of paired tissues/patients in Results 3.1), and the statistical approach is described broadly (t-tests/Wilcoxon/Cox) without clear multiple-comparison control across the many assays, which limits confidence in some claims (2.19 Statistical Analysis).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The key therapeutic claim is supported primarily by preclinical cell line and mouse xenograft experiments, so the overall study maps to Oxford LoE 5. Translational relevance is high because it targets a clinically used agent (Cetuximab) and proposes a mechanism of resistance with in vivo validation of sensitization when CAV2 is silenced (Abstract; Results 3.7). The clinical prognostic association work supports relevance but does not establish that modulating this axis improves patient outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: Key experimental components are described (human tissue sourcing/ethics, animal model setup and dosing, and core assay types including co-IP and ubiquitination assays) (Methods 2.1–2.3, 2.13–2.19). The manuscript reports the use of RNA-seq and TMT proteomics/IP-MS to nominate the pathway, but does not describe public deposition of these omics datasets in the normalized text, which reduces reproducibility (2.18; Results 3.4). Some reporting would benefit from clearer, consistent sample-size statements for patient materials and more explicit statistical reporting aligned to each figure/endpoint.

novelty_literature.justification: Positioning CAV2 as a modulator of Cetuximab sensitivity through ubiquitin-mediated disruption of the PACT-PKR axis appears to be a distinct mechanistic angle beyond a generic EGFR-pathway explanation (Abstract; Results 3.4–3.7). The inclusion of pathway rescue (co-depleting PACT or PKR to reverse sensitization) strengthens the novelty of the proposed causal chain (Results 3.7).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally organized with clear method and result subheadings that mirror the mechanistic progression from screening to validation and rescue. However, there is occasional repetition and some ambiguity/inconsistency in describing patient sample numbers and validation cohorts in the Results narrative, which makes it harder to follow the evidentiary chain without the supplementary tables/figures (Results 3.1). The abstract is broadly aligned to the claimed findings but compresses several heterogeneous data sources.

key_strengths: Multi-modal approach combining clinical association, in vitro functional assays, and in vivo xenograft validation of Cetuximab sensitization with CAV2 depletion (Methods 2.1–2.2; Results 3.2–3.7).
Mechanistic linkage supported by protein interaction/ubiquitination experiments and pathway rescue showing dependence on the PACT-PKR axis (Results 3.4–3.7).
Clear therapeutic focus on a clinically deployed EGFR antibody and a plausible resistance mechanism (Abstract; Results 3.7).
key_concerns: Narrative inconsistencies around clinical sample sizes/validation cohorts reduce confidence without clearer reconciliation in the main text (Results 3.1).
Statistical reporting is broad and does not clearly address multiplicity across the many assays/omics-derived hypotheses (2.19 Statistical Analysis).
Omics outputs (RNA-seq/proteomics) are described but not clearly made available in the normalized manuscript, limiting reproducibility (2.18; Results 3.4).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The mechanistic story and preclinical validation are compelling and clinically relevant, but the paper likely needs substantial tightening of cohort reporting, statistical transparency, and reproducibility statements to support acceptance at a mid-tier oncology venue.
